gaps.sentence: Although the road was blocked, we ___ reach the hospital in time.
gaps.explanation: For a single past achievement, 'was/were able to' is used, not 'could'.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have left the door unlocked — anyone could have walked in.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' blames someone for a past act: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid you ___ smoke anywhere in the terminal; it is strictly forbidden.
There ___ be a mistake — I ordered the vegetarian option.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses the speaker's certainty about a present situation: must be.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.
